fold_structure: production (12 x 30 days, step 30, min 56 days of history -> 7 folds evaluated)
window_meaning: training rows from the last N days before each origin; features use history < t only
selection_protocol: per fold k: the configuration with the lowest pooled WAPE over the folds BEFORE k (their test days all precede origin k); fold 1 evaluated uses R0_production

W30.hypothesis: only the newest regime (after the drop) is learned

W90.hypothesis: about one quarter of recent history

L1_no_sku.hypothesis: sku_code categorical with ~9.7k levels overfits SKU levels of the past

L2_regularized.hypothesis: simpler, more regularised trees generalise better across the level shift

L3_early_stop.hypothesis: 300 rounds is arbitrary; rounds chosen on the last 30 days BEFORE the origin (metric l1), then refit on the whole training window

L4_tweedie15.hypothesis: heavier zero mass suits intermittent daily demand

L5_l1.hypothesis: WAPE numerator = absolute error: the median objective optimises it directly

L6_trend.hypothesis: explicit recent-trend ratios (series and whole scope), from data < t only

L7_direct.hypothesis: recursive feedback of predicted means into lags/zero-share/days-since-sale inflates forecasts; a direct multi-horizon model (features at the origin + horizon) avoids it

L8_fallback14.hypothesis: fallback rates (intermittent / no model) adapt faster with a 14-day window

L9_recency60.hypothesis: all history is kept but older training rows count less (weight halves every 60 days before the origin), so the model follows the current level

C1_w90_nosku_reg.hypothesis: recent regime + no SKU identity + regularisation

C2_direct_nosku_reg.hypothesis: direct strategy + no SKU identity + regularisation

C3_w90_nosku_trend_es.hypothesis: recent regime + no SKU identity + trend features + early stopping
